# HEVC QP 74/75 regression vectors

These are synthetic project regression vectors, not official HEVC conformance vectors. `source.y4m` and `source-420.y4m` are 128×64, 12-bit 4:2:2 and 4:2:0 frames. Their planar samples are generated by:

- `Y[y,x] = (37*y + 53*x + 11*(y XOR x)) mod 4096`
- `Cb[y,x] = (71*y + 97*x + 233) mod 4096`
- `Cr[y,x] = (3*Cb[y,x] + 1701) mod 4096`

The bitstreams and reference Y4M files were generated with x265 `4.3+1-e9b8812`, built with 8/10/12-bit support. Both chroma formats used CQP, `--ipratio 1.0`, `--pbratio 1.0`, `--aq-mode 0`, `--no-cutree`, `--keyint 1`, `--min-keyint 1`, `--bframes 0`, and `--repeat-headers`. Input/output depth was 12; input chroma formats were `i422` and `i420`. Default Cb/Cr QP offsets are zero.

```sh
x265 --input source.y4m --output qp74.hevc --input-depth 12 --input-csp i422 \
  --output-depth 12 --qp 50 --ipratio 1.0 --pbratio 1.0 --aq-mode 0 \
  --no-cutree --keyint 1 --min-keyint 1 --bframes 0 --repeat-headers \
  --recon qp74.y4m --recon-depth 12 --log-level info
x265 --input source.y4m --output qp75.hevc --input-depth 12 --input-csp i422 \
  --output-depth 12 --qp 51 --ipratio 1.0 --pbratio 1.0 --aq-mode 0 \
  --no-cutree --keyint 1 --min-keyint 1 --bframes 0 --repeat-headers \
  --recon qp75.y4m --recon-depth 12 --log-level info

x265 --input source-420.y4m --output qp74-420.hevc --input-depth 12 --input-csp i420 \
  --output-depth 12 --qp 50 --ipratio 1.0 --pbratio 1.0 --aq-mode 0 \
  --no-cutree --keyint 1 --min-keyint 1 --bframes 0 --repeat-headers \
  --recon qp74-420.y4m --recon-depth 12 --log-level info
x265 --input source-420.y4m --output qp75-420.hevc --input-depth 12 --input-csp i420 \
  --output-depth 12 --qp 51 --ipratio 1.0 --pbratio 1.0 --aq-mode 0 \
  --no-cutree --keyint 1 --min-keyint 1 --bframes 0 --repeat-headers \
  --recon qp75-420.y4m --recon-depth 12 --log-level info
```

At 12-bit, `QpBdOffsetY` and `QpBdOffsetC` are both 24. For 4:2:2, coded QPs 50 and 51 produce qP′ 74 and 75 for Y, Cb, and Cr. For 4:2:0, luma qP′ is 74/75, while Table 8-10 maps chroma qPi 50/51 to 44/45 before the bit-depth offset, producing chroma qP′ 68/69. `bun test test/hevc-qp-boundary.test.ts` decodes all four streams as raw HEVC and synthetic `heix` items, comparing every component sample with x265's reconstruction. `heix` is used because Main 10 and Range Extensions profiles are outside the `heic` Main/Main Still Picture brand constraints in ISO/IEC 23008-12 Annex B.4.1.1.
